name: BorrowBox
top_fix: Add a real predict/observe loop to 05-PRACTICE (per-exercise expected error code + surviving state + a --filter command) and stop shipping two 'solutions' that are byte-identical to tests already committed in tests/BorrowBox.Infrastructure.Tests.
summary: Validate-and-construct-before-you-mutate, taught on a four-workflow repair where a bad expiry or due date used to strand equipment in Reserved/CheckedOut with no matching record. 29 tests match the TRX evidence exactly; limits (no DB transaction, no authz, no browser) are stated plainly. Dense unbroken prose and no red-first step are the weaknesses.

name: CampusOps
top_fix: Ship the pre-change files as astraupskill/snapshots/*.before.cs and add a step-0 exercise that restores them and reproduces the four PartStoreIsolationTests failures, so the claimed red-then-green story is something the learner performs.
summary: Model course. Two independent stores that could disagree become one commit boundary (ReserveForWorkOrderAsync under a single lock), reads and inserts become detached Snapshot() copies, and the inventory routes pick up the Operations policy they were missing. 42 tests match three TRX files exactly, with the 28-test baseline and the deliberately-red new tests both disclosed. Exercises 3-5 (idempotency, durable SQLite adapter, UI capstone) get reasoning, not code.

name: OpenSource_Upskilling_.Ramp (Expense Management)
top_fix: Fix 03-WORKED-CHANGE.md:3 - with BoundedChannelFullMode.Wait a discarded WriteAsync does not drop the item, it parks a pending writer; explain the real bug (lost exception + lost back-pressure + ordering) and add BoundedChannelFullMode to 02-CONCEPTS.
summary: Per-expense gate shared by commands and the reimbursement worker, non-blocking TryEnqueue admission before the status transition, and a genuine security fix: CanSystemTransition used to allow the worker any legal edge including manager-only approval. Ten new xUnit facts (the project had none) assert unchanged state after rejection; VERIFICATION even discloses the lock-dictionary leak Astra introduced. One wrong claim about Channel.WriteAsync semantics and no database anywhere.

name: OpenSource_Upskilling_.Stripe (Subscription Billing Workshop)
top_fix: Add a prerequisites/sequencing box splitting the course into Part 1 (CRUD, pagination, validation - exercises 1-4) and Part 2 (concurrency, receipts, outbox - exercises 5-7), and add a red-first exercise that restores docs/original/src/.../BillingStore.cs.txt and records which of the 66 tests fail.
summary: The batch capstone: a rebuilt billing simulator with SQLite persistence, workspace tenancy and three roles, full CRUD over seven entities, SQL pagination/search, strong-ETag If-Match (428 when absent) and a single-transaction authorize/receipt/mutate/audit boundary in BillingStore.Write. 66 xUnit/HTTP tests and 15 named browser workflows with matching evidence files and reviewed screenshots. Because it is a rebuild there is no broken code to repair, and the last three exercises are senior design work with a rubric instead of answers.

name: MeterForge
top_fix: Add a section mapping ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd onto its database equivalent - UNIQUE (tenant_id, external_event_id) plus INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING * - since the pattern is taught entirely in memory.
summary: Best-taught course in the batch and the right introduction to idempotency. A check-then-act race (TryAdd with a discarded boolean) becomes GetOrAdd returning the stored winner, a payload mismatch under the same key becomes HTTP 409 instead of a silent success, and two real ASP.NET pipeline bugs around X-Trace-Id and Problem Details correlation get fixed and explained. Per-chapter time estimates, a prediction notebook, exercises with traps; 51 tests match four TRX files exactly and the limits volunteer an O(n) scan Astra introduced.

name: MissionControl / FleetCommand
top_fix: Add a SQLite-locking section to 02-CONCEPTS: SqlitePragmaInterceptor.cs:10 sets WAL + busy_timeout=5000 and BeginTransactionAsync(Serializable) becomes BEGIN IMMEDIATE, which is what stops the four-way concurrency test throwing SQLITE_BUSY - none of which is currently mentioned.
summary: The only course here teaching CRUD on a real ORM against a real database, and its EF Core statements are correct where most get them wrong (change tracking is not a transaction; rollback does not un-mutate a tracked entity; a global query filter is stronger than an existence check). Closes an unvalidated ProjectId write that could point a task at another workspace's project, and proves serializable ticket allocation with four parallel HTTP requests asserting 1,2,3,4. 139 tests match both TRX files. Thin at 5,136 words for an app this large.

name: Master 6 (LMS monorepo)
top_fix: Add implement-it exercises with acceptance contracts (all nine are currently predict-and-explain) and replace the Proxy-over-the-same-mock $transaction fixture with one that can fail, since the atomicity claim currently rests on asserting that $transaction was called.
summary: Best JS/TS course in the batch for multi-tenant authorization. Fixes textbook IDOR: an x-organization-id header trusted without checking memberships, a lesson-progress update with no ownership filter at all, and an enroll route that took the newest course version even when it was a draft. Audit and outbox writes now share the business write's Prisma transaction client. 29 tests match the logs and the README states up front that mocked-Prisma tests prove call grouping, not rollback. apps/web (Next 15) and apps/worker have zero tests and are never discussed.

name: jstrain2.3 (Knowledge Workspace)
top_fix: Add a TypeScript chapter/exercise - the project is 100% plain JS/.mjs with only a jsconfig.json, so half the target stack is absent; converting workspaceSchema.mjs and databaseModel.mjs to typed modules would show which of the 97 runtime checks become compile-time guarantees.
summary: The strongest JavaScript course here: it teaches the gap between what React rendered, what the user typed, what IndexedDB kept and what SQLite committed. Bearer auth, whole-document validation and revision-checked atomic writes on the server; per-tab drafts, no auto-replay of uncertain writes and explicit three-way conflict review on the client. 97 Node tests match the run log file by file and 25 named Playwright workflows drive the production server against a throwaway database, including a bug the harness found late plus its regression. No TypeScript, no time estimates, and the last two exercises are senior design work with outlines only.
